prompt_text: Who is the best marketing agency in Maryland?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” marketing agency for everyone — it depends on what you need. To give you a useful recommendation I need a few details. Meanwhile, here’s how to find the best match and what I can do next.

Quick questions
- What type of marketing do you need most? (digital/SEO/PPC/social/branding/PR/content/lead gen/marketing automation/etc.)
- What’s your industry or target audience?
- Company size and annual marketing budget (rough range)?
- Are you looking for a local Maryland agency (in a specific city) or ok with remote/national agencies?
- Timeline and KPIs (brand awareness, leads, sales, installs, etc.)?

How I’ll pick the “best” for you
I’ll evaluate agencies based on the things that matter for results:
- Relevant industry experience and case studies
- Clear, measurable KPIs and ROI examples
- Size and skill mix (in-house vs contractors)
- Technology stack (analytics, CRM, ad platforms)
- Client retention and references
- Pricing model and contract terms
- Cultural fit and communication style

Where to look / quick resources
- Clutch.co and G2 (client reviews, portfolios)
- LinkedIn and agency websites (case studies)
- Local chapters: American Marketing Association (AMA) MD chapters, Baltimore/DC business journals
- Word of mouth: ask peers in your industry

What to ask agencies (short list)
- Can you show case studies with outcomes (traffic, leads, revenue) for businesses like mine?
- Who will be on my team and how do we communicate?
- What metrics will you report and how often?
- What upfront work and ongoing work do you expect from my team?
- Can I speak with existing clients or see contract templates?

Red flags
- Vague promises (“we’ll get you to the top of Google” with no plan)
- No measurable case studies or unwillingness to share references
- Long, inflexible contracts without performance clauses

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a tailored shortlist of 4–6 Maryland agencies (or remote agencies that commonly work with MD companies) based on your answers above
- Draft an RFP or interview checklist you can send to agencies

Tell me the quick answers to those questions and I’ll put together a short, prioritized list.
